It drifts serenely past the tiny ship, vast and unhurried, its shadow swallowing the vessel whole before releasing it back into the light.
A single immense tendril reaches slowly toward the tiny craft, its tip brightening as the gap closes, the moment suspended and wordless.
It turns a cluster of glassy eyes toward the viewer, light blooming across its surface as recognition, slow and enormous, begins to form.
It feeds on a nearby star, ribbons of plasma drawn upward into its translucent body, pooling like gold in its deep luminous core.
It begins to uncoil, vast segment after segment unfurling into open space, the motion unhurried, the scale only becoming clear after long seconds.
A pulse of cold blue light travels the full length of its body, then repeats, then varies, a rhythm that feels unmistakably like language.
It releases a slow cloud of smaller glowing forms, each one drifting outward like a breath released, surrounding the tiny ship without touching it.
It rises from the cloud-tops of the gas giant below, crown first, then shoulder, then the impossible rest of it, trailing storm and silence.
It rotates slowly to face the camera, the turn taking minutes, its attention arriving like weather, like the turning of a tide.
It threads between the debris field with impossible delicacy, each enormous limb placed with care, as if aware of every fragment in its path.
It passes through the planetary rings, ice and rock parting around its body, the disturbance gentle, almost considerate, a colossus moving softly through glass.
It curls protectively around the small cold moon, its body forming a loose and luminous cradle, the gesture ancient and unmistakably tender.
It pulses in slow rhythm, expanding and contracting across its whole vast surface, the cadence steady, like breathing, like the patience of deep time.
It emits a long sustained tone of light, shifting through frequencies visible and not, the signal washing over the ship and continuing outward forever.
It feeds on the edge of the nebula, drawing color and ionized gas into itself, its body brightening in blooms of violet and copper.
One enormous eye drifts to rest directly on the ship, the pupil widening slowly, the recognition in it vast and entirely unhurried.
It unfurls a single translucent membrane, spreading it wide against the starfield, the structure catching light like a sail made of stained glass.
It holds perfectly still, every filament and tendril suspended, as though listening, the whole of its impossible body suddenly and completely attentive.
A cluster of smaller glowing forms detach and spiral toward the ship, circling it slowly, examining, reporting back to the vast patient body above.
It passes the ship so closely that its skin fills every window, its surface moving like a slow deep current, lit from somewhere within.
It tilts its great head and the light across its body rearranges itself into something that resembles, almost unbearably, a face looking back.
It draws a long filament of nebula light into its mouth, tasting it, then turns its gaze toward the ship as if comparing.
It wraps loosely around the wreckage of an old satellite, its grip careful, preserving the shape of it, studying the thing humans made.
It exhales a slow expansion of bioluminescent particles that drift and settle around the ship like snow, each point of light dimly pulsing.
It simply stops, directly before the ship, and waits, its whole body softly glowing, offering the first silence that has ever felt like an answer.
